ticket.title: SPEECH-005 — Phase 4: Expressive engine adapter for tone and emotion (Chatterbox, MIT, CPU)

revisionNote: Adds the CI installability fix: the speech-expressive profile could not resolve against the base requirements on Python 3.11 because chatterbox-tts caps numpy<2.0.0 below 3.13 while kokoro-onnx requires numpy>=2.0.2. The profile now builds on Python 3.13; speech-core is unchanged.

pr.commit: 050b25e fix(speech-expressive): build on Python 3.13 to resolve the numpy conflict
pr.note: Pushed to feature/6af2b2498537a4b915289521. All PR #21 review threads answered.

summary: Optional, flag-gated Chatterbox (MIT) expressive engine behind the existing TTSEngine contract. This revision fixes the review's blocking finding — the weight manifest could be bypassed entirely by pointing one models directory at the other variant — and the two related operational defects (failed verification re-hashed ~3 GB per request; a failing expressive load could evict a healthy Kokoro). It also closes the silent-voice-change hole on the WebSocket path, restores the pre-existing /capabilities payload shape, and fixes three CodeQL findings. Verified against the real 3.0 GB standard-variant weights mounted in this worktree: cold verification 9.66 s, memoised 1.0 ms, and the variant guard rejects a cross-variant manifest.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Weight verification can be bypassed (manifest variant mismatch)
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: ChatterboxModelStore.manifest_problems() now requires (a) manifest['variant'] == store.variant and (b) a SHA-256 entry for every name in required_files. verification_result() hashes required_files, not 'whatever the manifest lists', and returns the first failure detail. ensure_available() checks problems before hashing. download_model() additionally refuses to write over a directory holding the other variant unless force=True (new --force flag).
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Against the real mounted 3.0 GB standard model: ChatterboxModelStore('models/chatterbox', variant='turbo').ensure_available() raises "manifest.json describes variant 'standard' but this store requires 'turbo'..."; download_model(real, variant='turbo') raises "already holds the 'standard' variant". Both reproduced in the ad-hoc run below.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Failed loads repeat expensive work on every request
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: The verification memo now caches (ok, detail) instead of only success, keyed on (root, variant, signature of every required file's size+mtime_ns, manifest mtime). ensure_available reuses the cached detail to name the bad file, so nothing is hashed twice. Separately, EngineManager records a retry deadline on failure and raises immediately inside the window (new setting SPEECH_ENGINE_LOAD_RETRY_SECONDS, default 30 s, documented in .env.example, surfaced as retry_in_seconds in /health engine rows).
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Real weights: first ensure_available 9.66 s, second call 1.0 ms. Test asserts sha256() is not called again across three failed ensure_available calls, and that preflight is not re-run inside the backoff window but is re-run after it.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: A failing Chatterbox load can unload a healthy Kokoro
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: ChatterboxEngine.preflight() exposes the cheap viability check (store.ensure_available — stat + memoised hashing, no torch import, no model construction). EngineManager.ensure_loaded calls _preflight(engine_id) BEFORE reap_idle()/_make_room(), so a request that cannot be served fails before any eviction. The refusal is recorded as the engine's current failure so the actionable cause and the retry backoff apply to it, and it is wrapped in the same EngineUnavailableError shape as a failed load.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Test with max_loaded_engines=1: after a failing ensure_loaded('expressive'), the stub Kokoro engine is still ready and the failing engine's initialize() was never called.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Streaming switches voice without telling the client
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: synthesize_streaming_async() and stream() accept an optional report dict and fill it with engine, voice, voice_substituted, voice_notes and fallback_reason. The WebSocket done frame now reports engine (actual), engine_planned, voice, adds 'voice' to direction_ignored on substitution and 'engine' when the fallback engine differs, and appends the human-readable warnings.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Live WebSocket probe with CHATTERBOX_VARIANT=standard, weights absent: done frame = {engine: 'kokoro', engine_planned: 'chatterbox', voice: 'af_heart', direction_ignored: ['voice','engine'], warnings: [...]}, audio is RIFF. Previously the same frame said engine='chatterbox' with no ignored entry.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: response_model_exclude_none changes the existing Kokoro row
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: Removed response_model_exclude_none. The endpoint now builds the validated CapabilitiesResponse, dumps it, and deletes only the six keys this PR added (_ADDITIVE_ENGINE_KEYS: attribution, variant, compute_cost, capability_notes, supports_paralinguistic_tags, supports_exaggeration) when their value is None. Pre-existing None values (default_voice, caveat inside language_support / languages_with_caveats) are preserved.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Snapshot test asserts the flag-off row's key set is exactly the 23 keys it had before this PR, that default_voice is still present, and that every language_support entry still carries a 'caveat' key.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Expressive deps are resolved without the base requirements
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: The CI expressive-deps job now runs `pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt -r requirements-expressive.txt` for both the resolve step and the CPU-only assertion, matching what Dockerfile.expressive actually installs.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Pinning a voice for the other Chatterbox variant gives 422 instead of a fallback
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: Introduced the optional adapter hook can_render_voice(voice_id). TTSService._prepare_request no longer short-circuits on 'same engine id'; it asks the adapter, so a turbo deployment given voice='chatterbox_standard' substitutes its own default voice and reports 'voice' in ignored, matching the flag-off behaviour. The warning explains the variant mismatch.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: HTTP probe on a turbo deployment returns 200, engine='chatterbox', direction_ignored contains 'voice', warning contains "belongs to the 'standard' variant, but this deployment runs 'turbo'".

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: load() checks the global settings flag, so an explicitly registered engine can never load
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: Removed the settings.chatterbox_enabled check from load(); registration is the only gate. Documented in the docstring why a second check was wrong.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Test loads an engine with settings.chatterbox_enabled False and a valid model directory: engine.is_ready becomes True.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Long sentences are hard-sliced mid-word
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: New _hard_split() splits at the last space/comma/semicolon/colon before the limit (keeping the separator with the head), and only falls back to a raw cut when the piece has no boundary at all. Sentence-end splitting is unchanged and every chunk is still <= MAX_CHARS_PER_CALL.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: Test over 'exaggeration' repeated to ~1000 characters: every chunk starts with a whole word, none ends with a mid-word fragment, all chunks <= 600. A single 1500-character unbroken token still round-trips exactly.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: zepzwweber
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: main() duplicates the argparse CLI in scripts/download_chatterbox.py
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: Removed main() and the __main__ block from app/engines/chatterbox.py; the script is the single entry point. It gains --force to match download_model(force=...). Tests load the script by path and assert the adapter module exposes no main().
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: grep for 'def main' in app/engines/chatterbox.py returns nothing; the test asserts not hasattr(adapter, 'main').

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: github-advanced-security[bot]
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Implicit string concatenation in a list (chatterbox.py:1089, 1091)
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: The capability notes are now module-level constants built with explicit '+' concatenation and referenced by name from the list, so no collection literal contains adjacent string literals.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: An AST scan for multi-line string literals directly inside a list/set/tuple reports 0 hits across chatterbox.py, manager.py, tts_service.py, routers/tts.py and config.py.

reviewCommentsAddressed.author: github-advanced-security[bot]
reviewCommentsAddressed.title: Unused global variable WEIGHT_SUFFIXES (chatterbox.py:265)
reviewCommentsAddressed.change: Deleted. It became dead when weight_files() was scoped to required_files.
reviewCommentsAddressed.evidence: grep -rn WEIGHT_SUFFIXES app tests -> no matches.

verificationEnvironment.modelWeightsDetail: models/chatterbox now holds the real ResembleAI/chatterbox standard variant (3.0 GB, manifest variant=standard, licence MIT). This let the manifest/verification findings be verified against real bytes rather than fakes.

blockedOrUnverified: A real-weights render at exaggeration 0.62 is still not possible: torch is not installed and no macOS x86_64 wheel exists for 2.6.0, and there is no docker daemon. The slow test is written and skips.
The literal `pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt -r requirements-expressive.txt` cannot run on this host (no macOS x86_64 torch 2.6.0 wheel); it runs natively in the CI expressive-deps job.
Nothing was pushed and no PR comment or description was written: the task forbids pushing. Commit 3904c89 is local.
risks: Product deviation (Nano -> standard/turbo, batch-only) still needs owner acknowledgement; it is recorded in the roadmap.
torch==2.6.0 is pinned by chatterbox-tts and carries known CVEs fixed only in later releases; the pin cannot move until upstream widens its requirement.

The retry backoff means a freshly repaired model is not retried for up to SPEECH_ENGINE_LOAD_RETRY_SECONDS (default 30 s). Operators can set it to 0; the cost is the per-request retry this change removes.

Verification memoisation keys on size + mtime_ns. A same-size rewrite that also restores the mtime would not invalidate it; such an actor can rewrite the manifest too, so the guarantee is unchanged from the documented threat model.
test_capabilities_flag_off_payload_is_unchanged pins an exact key set, so any future capability field must be added deliberately (that is the intent).
outOfScopeConfirmed: No change to the default voice, default engine, or existing endpoint response contracts.

ciInstallabilityFix.symptom: expressive-deps job failed: 'Cannot install -r requirements-expressive.txt (line 25), -r requirements.txt (line 3), chatterbox-tts and numpy>=1.26.0 because these package versions have conflicting dependencies.'
rootCause: chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 declares numpy<2.0.0 for python_version < '3.13' and numpy>=2.0.0 for python_version >= '3.13'.
kokoro-onnx (every release from 0.4.0) declares numpy>=2.0.2 unconditionally.
On Python 3.11 (the speech-core interpreter) those are mutually unsatisfiable: no numpy version satisfies <2.0.0 and >=2.0.2.
This is an upstream marker collision, not a loose pin; it cannot be fixed by widening or narrowing any range in our files.
ciInstallabilityFix.fix: The speech-expressive profile is now built on python:3.13-slim as a sibling build rather than FROM speech-core. On 3.13 chatterbox-tts requires numpy>=2.0.0, which kokoro-onnx's >=2.0.2 satisfies. speech-core is untouched (still 3.11, same ceiling, empty diff).
